status_rationale: Echelon has no production deployment; the relevant rules exist only in the proposed Secure Construction Standard v0.1 or Unbound requirements, so this is a target state.
target_answer: Echelon builds all products under an adopted secure development standard that maps every practice to NIST SSDF tasks, measures maturity against OWASP SAMM annually, and enforces most practices as automated gates whose results are retained as evidence. title: Code review and independent verification of changes
status_rationale: Echelon has no production deployment; the relevant rules exist only in the proposed Secure Construction Standard v0.1 or Unbound requirements, so this is a target state.
target_answer: Every change is reviewed by someone other than its author; changes to control-relevant modules (gate, ledger, reservations, holds, authority, dispatch) need two approvers, neither the author; an AI agent is never the sole reviewer of agent-authored code; review records and automated check results are retained per change. Review focuses on design and invariants; mechanical weakness detection is delegated to automated gates. Second person: until Echelon hires a second engineer, the independent reviewer is a contracted external code reviewer (a named individual or firm under contract, with its own source control account bound to branch protection). An AI agent never counts as the second reviewer. As of 2026-11-25 no reviewer is contracted, so this control has no operator; the compensating position is disclosure of single-maintainer status and periodic external review of control-relevant diffs once contracted.
current_practice: Not established for a product. Limen's CODEOWNERS (limen@743cdb9b:.github/CODEOWNERS) requires the single repository owner's review for guardrail paths; no two-person review is evidenced.
intended_practice: Every change is reviewed by someone other than its author; changes to control-relevant modules (gate, ledger, reservations, holds, authority, dispatch) need two approvers, neither the author; an AI agent is never the sole reviewer of agent-authored code; review records and automated check results are retained per change. Review focuses on design and invariants; mechanical weakness detection is delegated to automated gates.
provable: Nothing for a production service; no Echelon production system exists as of 2026-11-25.
customer_statement: Echelon intends to implement this as part of Unbound's initial build; it is not in operation today and no evidence is available yet.
open_questions: How will two-approver review be met if Echelon has one human engineer? Not established.

challenge.customer_intent: Prevent malicious or careless code from reaching production unseen.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Backdoor, logic bomb or vulnerability introduced by one actor.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Peer review catches some defects and deters insiders, but reviewers miss most injection-class bugs and rubber-stamping is common; effectiveness depends on reviewer independence and attention.
challenge.legally_required: No; PCI DSS 6.2.3 requires review of bespoke code for card environments only.
challenge.contractually_required: Commonly asked and expected by SOC 2 auditors under CC8.1.
challenge.historical_convention: Pull request approval by one peer.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Weakness classes removed structurally need less reviewer attention; review can concentrate on invariants and authority.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Branch protection, required checks, module tagging that raises approval count.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Structural restriction plus automated gates plus human review of control-relevant changes only, with AI review as an addition.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: A single human with administrative rights over branch protection can bypass the control.
challenge.alternative_cost: Gate engineering plus external reviewer retainer if headcount is insufficient.
challenge.alternative_risks: Overreliance on AI review that shares the authoring model's blind spots.
supporting_arguments: Concentrates scarce human attention where it matters.

agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Uncertain; auditors expect independent human review and segregation regardless of team size.'; institutional acceptance rating 'uncertain' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Independence is the point of the control and cannot be automated away.
Small team cannot meet two-approver rule today.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: Security testing integrated into the development pipeline
status_rationale: Echelon has no production deployment; the relevant rules exist only in the proposed Secure Construction Standard v0.1 or Unbound requirements, so this is a target state.

title: Developer security training and agent security instructions
status_rationale: Echelon has no production deployment; the relevant rules exist only in the proposed Secure Construction Standard v0.1 or Unbound requirements, so this is a target state.
target_answer: Human developers complete role-based secure development training at onboarding and annually, with completion recorded. AI coding agents operate under versioned security instructions and tool restrictions that are evaluated against known-vulnerable tasks when changed. Because most weakness classes are removed structurally, training emphasizes authority, invariants and threat modeling over syntax-level rules.

title: Language choice and memory safety
status_rationale: Echelon has no production deployment; the relevant rules exist only in the proposed Secure Construction Standard v0.1 or Unbound requirements, so this is a target state.
target_answer: Application code is F# on .NET, a memory-safe, bounds-checked runtime; unsafe code and unreviewed native interop are disabled by compiler configuration and inventoried per build; non-F# code (the TypeScript Limen kernel, interop glue) is minimal, listed and reviewed. Echelon states plainly that memory safety does not prevent logic, authorization, arithmetic or denial-of-service defects, nor defects in the runtime and native dependencies, and that F# has a smaller security tooling and talent ecosystem, which it compensates for with structural rules and custom analyzers.
current_practice: Echelon tool repositories are F# and .NET with warnings as errors. Limen's browser kernel is TypeScript and its WebAssembly site includes a small C# JSExport marshalling file. No product exists.

challenge.legally_required: No; CISA and partner agencies recommend memory-safe languages as guidance.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Eliminates memory corruption in managed code within scope; not in the runtime, native libraries or interop.
challenge.stronger_alternative: F# with exhaustive matching and validated types adds logic-level safety beyond C#.
